topics.label: Introduction and lecture learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the introductory framing and sets the learning objectives for the lecture.

topics.label: Cancer etiology, genetic predisposition, and environmental epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the foundational causes of cancer by examining the relative contributions of intrinsic genetic factors, random mutations, and environmental exposures.

topics.label: Infectious agents and viral oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious pathogens, particularly Epstein-Barr virus in the context of Burkitt lymphoma, drive oncogenesis.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical and physical mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how physical radiation and chemical carcinogens cause DNA damage directly or through metabolic activation into reactive intermediates.

topics.label: Tumour promotion and host susceptibility in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how non-mutagenic promoter agents, chronic inflammation, and host developmental susceptibility cooperate with initiators to facilitate cancer development.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying carcinogens and evaluating cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics present the experimental, genomic, and epidemiological approaches used to identify carcinogens and assess exposure risks.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic delivers the lecturer's final summary and concluding remarks.
